title: Model Training Recipe Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Reproducible training configurations, datasets, hyperparameters, and evaluation results. The Model Training Recipe Database turns model training from folklore into reproducible records. Each recipe is a complete, checkable configuration: dataset composition and preprocessing, optimizer and schedule, hyperparameters, hardware setup, and the evaluation results it produced. A recipe that cannot be re-run is marked incomplete — reproducibility is the entry ticket, not a bonus.

title: Model Training Recipe Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Training recipe anatomy. Data: composition weights, dedup method (MinHash/LSH), filtering rules, tokenizer and vocab size. Optimization: AdamW update m_t = beta1*m_{t-1}+(1-beta1)*g_t; v_t = beta2*v_{t-1}+(1-beta2)*g_t^2; theta -= lr * m_hat/(sqrt(v_hat)+eps) - lr*lambda*theta. Schedule: warmup then cosine decay lr(t) = lr_min + 0.5*(lr_max-lr_min)*(1+cos(pi*t/T)). Stability: loss spikes correlate with lr too high for batch size; rule of thumb lr scales with sqrt(batch) up to limits. Evaluation: perplexity on held-out sets, plus task benchmarks; record evals at checkpoints, not just the end, to catch divergence early.

title: Model Training Recipe Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: completeness test (no missing required fields); consistency test (weights sum to 1, schedule endpoints match); eval-schema test (results use the standard metric names and units); failure-recipe test (known-bad configs are flagged before use). Limitations: recipes are hardware-sensitive; reported results are as-published; data-mix ablations are expensive so coverage is partial. Every recipe carries provenance: who ran it, on what, when.

demo.title: Verification: calibration error (ECE)
demo.code: const pairs=[[0.9,1],[0.9,1],[0.9,0],[0.6,1],[0.6,0],[0.6,0]];const bins={};pairs.forEach(([c,ok])=>{const b=Math.round(c*10)/10;(bins[b]=bins[b]||{n:0,c:0,conf:0});bins[b].n++;bins[b].c+=ok;bins[b].conf+=c;});let ece=0;for(const b in bins){const B=bins[b];ece+=Math.abs(B.c/B.n-B.conf/B.n)*(B.n/pairs.length);}J({ece:+ece.toFixed(3)});assert(ece>0&&ece<1,'ece');
